title: Network Node Security Strategy
definition: The dual-layered defense strategy used in a headless network to maintain health, consisting of Hard Security and Soft Security.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a city with two security systems: one that uses locks and alarms (Hard Security) and another that relies on the behavior of its citizens (Soft Security). Together, they keep the city safe.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A network node security strategy involves a combination of Hard Security (cryptographic enforcement) and Soft Security (social dynamics and Proof of Service) to ensure network integrity and robustness.
difficulty_levels.expert: The network node security strategy is a dual-layered defense system that combines Hard Security (cryptographic enforcement) and Soft Security (social dynamics, gossip, and Proof of Service) to maintain network health. Hard Security includes mandatory signatures and Proof-of-Work, while Soft Security amplifies security through social dynamics and cooperative behavior. The strategy provides resilience against Sybil attacks and high-level coordination attacks, while also allowing for a scalable and decentralized network.

extra_fields.insight: The use of a dual-layered defense strategy in network node security, combining Hard Security (cryptographic enforcement) and Soft Security (social dynamics and Proof of Service), provides network health and robustness while allowing for a scalable and decentralized network.
